title: Nacar v. Gallery Frames
summary: The Supreme Court revised the guidelines on the imposition of legal interest rates, aligning them with BSP Circular No. 799 which reduced the legal interest rate from 12% to 6% per annum. This case became the controlling authority for the computation of legal interest in all money claims.
doctrine: Effective July 1, 2013, the legal interest rate for loans or forbearance of money is 6% per annum (previously 12%). For obligations not constituting a loan or forbearance of money, the rate is also 6% per annum. Once a judgment becomes final, the total amount shall earn interest at 6% per annum until full satisfaction.
fullText:
PERALTA, J.:

The Court takes this opportunity to settle, once and for all, the proper imposition of legal interest rates.

With the advent of BSP-MB Circular No. 799, effective July 1, 2013, the rate of interest for the loan or forbearance of any money, goods, or credits and the rate allowed in judgments, in the absence of an express contract as to such rate of interest, shall be six percent (6%) per annum.

The guidelines for the computation of legal interest are hereby modified as follows: (1) When the obligation is breached, and it consists in the payment of a sum of money, the interest due should be that which may have been stipulated in writing. (2) In the absence of stipulation, the rate of interest shall be 6% per annum.
